reason: Elasticsearch keeps soft-deleted documents (updates, deletes) and delete tombstones in its segments, through merges too, while retention leases hold them, and docFreq counts them; roll drops deleted documents when it merges. The term suggester's freq differs after updates or deletes once roll merged.

The phrase suggester's WordScorer uses maxDoc as the term count on multi-segment shards; Elasticsearch's maxDoc includes soft-delete tombstones (one per delete) and retained soft-deleted documents, roll's does not (see the term suggester entry).
As POST _search .suggest.p[].options[].score: the tombstones in Elasticsearch's maxDoc lower the candidates' scores, which can drop a correction below the input's score (or lift one above it).
A missing scroll context's reason names the context id, which differs by nature (Elasticsearch prints its internal [uuid][counter] form).

As POST _search .suggest.p[].options[].score: significant_terms' superset size is the shard's maxDoc and a keyword term's background frequency its docFreq. On Elasticsearch both count a soft-delete tombstone per delete (even of a missing document; maxDoc only) and the soft-deleted documents that merges retain; roll's count deleted documents only until it merges them away (any typed_keys name, nesting or _msearch item).
